data.title: Water Flow
data.statement:
Here at Water-Generating Cells™ Corporation, we sell cells that generate water to our clients and fill whatever holes they have so they can make lakes, pools, miniature waterfalls, and similar features, with ease. We are trying to offer an experience where the client can see what their body of water would look like before we deliver and apply the cells. That's where you come in.

You will be given the dimensions and the 2-dimensional ASCII representation of the client's area, which contains at least one water-generating cell {{o}}. It generates a water stream {{~}} (tilde) that initially only goes downward, but will stop and start flooding at row [[r]] (0-based).

<<Terrains>>

When a falling stream encounters a cell, its behavior depends on the character in that cell:

{{.}} is an empty space. The stream enters it and continues downward.

{{_}} is a flat terrain. The stream spreads in two directions, left and right, on the row immediately above the terrain. In each direction, the stream continues spreading until it can continue downward again, or until the path is blocked.

{{^}} is a sharp terrain. The stream splits into two branches, which enters the cells immediately to the left and right of the terrain. Both branches then continue downward. A branch is created only if the destination cell is empty, as well as the one directly above it.

{{|}} is a thin wall. It results in the same two-way split as {{^}}. An exception is that when either or both branches are blocked, the wall becomes waterlogged ({{!}}), and the stream continues downward in the unblocked branch (if any). In case there is another thin wall beneath, that one will only be waterlogged and the stream will not split.

{{#}} is a thick wall. The stream simply stops.

{{\}} and {{/}} are slopes. The stream moves to the cell immediately left of {{/}} and immediately right of {{\}} before continuing downward.

<<Obstructions>>

{{.}} is the only ordinary cell that a stream can enter. When entered by a stream, it becomes {{~}}. A thin wall {{|}} that is waterlogged becomes {{!}} and can also be traversed by a downward stream (but does not become {{~}}).

A stream cannot enter any cell containing terrain, another stream, or a water-generating cell. The boundary of the area is also treated as an obstruction. The only exceptions are empty cells {{.}} and waterlogged thin walls {{!}}, which are handled as described above.

If a stream attempts to enter an obstructed cell, that stream ceases to exist.

<<Flooding>>

If a stream reaches row [[r]], it becomes flood water. Flood water attempts to spread to the four neighboring cells (up, down, left, right), entering only {{.}} cells. Flooding is limited to row [[r]] and below; flood water cannot spread above row [[r]]. Thin walls {{|}} are not waterlogged when inside the flood water.

<<Task>>

Your task is to output the final state of the client's area after all streams have been generated by the water-generating cells and have interacted with the various features in the area.

Cell is below the flood level

Terrains

When a falling stream encounters a cell, its behavior depends on the character in that cell:

. is an empty space. The stream enters it and continues downward.

_ is a flat terrain. The stream spreads in two directions, left and right, on the row immediately above the terrain. In each direction, the stream continues spreading until it can continue downward again, or until the path is blocked.

An exception is that when either or both branches are blocked, the wall becomes waterlogged (!), and the stream continues downward in the unblocked branch (if any). In case there is another thin wall beneath, that one will only be waterlogged and the stream will not split.

# is a thick wall. The stream simply stops.

\ and / are slopes. The stream moves to the cell immediately left of / and immediately right of \ before continuing downward.

. is the only ordinary cell that a stream can enter. When entered by a stream, it becomes ~. A thin wall | that is waterlogged becomes ! and can also be traversed by a downward stream (but does not become ~).

A stream cannot enter any cell containing terrain, another stream, or a water-generating cell. The boundary of the area is also treated as an obstruction. The only exceptions are empty cells . and waterlogged thin walls !, which are handled as described above.

If a stream attempts to enter an obstructed cell, that stream ceases to exist.

Flooding

If a stream reaches row r, it becomes flood water. Flood water attempts to spread to the four neighboring cells (up, down, left, right), entering only . cells. Flooding is limited to row r and below; flood water cannot spread above row r. Thin walls | are not waterlogged when inside the flood water.

Task

Your task is to output the final state of the client's area after all streams have been generated by the water-generating cells and have interacted with the various features in the area.
Input
Line 1: The width of the grid.
Line 2: The height of the grid.
Line 3: The row in which water starts flooding.
Next h lines: A two-dimensional ASCII representation of the client's area, with w characters for each line.
Output
h lines: w characters for each line, showing what the two-dimensional grid will look like after the water-generating cells' effect.
Constraints
0 <= w <= 30
0 <= h <= 30
0 <= r <= h
There is going to be at least one water-generating cell o in the grid.
Example
Input
5
8
3

|...|

Output
|.o.|
|.~.|
